neighbours.label: then-versus-now contrast: the word right before 'now'/'today' when the present is set against an earlier time
fire: Bread cost far less in my childhood than it does now.
The village was much smaller fifty years ago than it is today.
Teachers had more freedom back then than they have now.
Few people owned cars in 1920, unlike the millions we see today.
Radio was once as popular as television is today.
My grandfather earned less in a year than I earn now.
The river was cleaner a century ago than it is now.
Phones were huge in the eighties compared to the ones we carry today.
quiet: Bread costs three dollars at the bakery on our street.
The village is small and quiet in the winter.
Teachers have a meeting every Friday after school.
Many people own cars in this part of the country.
Radio is a good way to hear the local news.
My grandfather earns a pension from the railway.
The river is wide and slow near the town.
Phones are not allowed in the exam room.

predictions: then-vs-now comparisons fire on the verb/adjective before 'now/today'; plain present statements with the same words stay quiet
notes: Probe: 'than they do now' 0.630, 'company it is today' 0.374, 'popular thirty years ago' 0.356, 'higher than it is now' 0.294, 'trees we see today' 0.229; 'have a lot of power in this city' 0.007, 'is famous for' 0.010, 'We see the trees' 0.052.
